subject.title: WhatsApp QR-unavailable/headless login needs phone-code fallback

question: Should WhatsApp phone-code login be exposed through the generic channel login contract and `openclaw channels login --phone-number`, or should the entrypoint stay WhatsApp-owned?
rationale: The remaining work is not just a Baileys implementation detail: the open PRs expand public CLI/plugin-auth surface and change persisted WhatsApp auth-state classification.

options.title: Accept Generic Login Method After Fix
options.body: Keep the typed generic login-method or phone-number path, but require the Baileys pairing-code fix, QR compatibility, and live/upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Move To WhatsApp-Owned Surface
options.body: Rework the fallback so phone-code login stays local to the WhatsApp plugin without expanding the generic channel-auth contract.

options.title: Pause Until Dependency Path Is Proven
options.body: Keep the issue open but wait for stronger Baileys pairing-code proof or upstream hardening before committing to a public entrypoint.

recommendation.title: Accept Generic Login Method After Fix
recommendation.body: Keep the typed generic login-method or phone-number path, but require the Baileys pairing-code fix, QR compatibility, and live/upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision crosses public CLI, plugin SDK, docs, and channel-auth boundaries where recent history points to steipete as the strongest routing owner.
